Name: Durumi Hut - Harvest Helpers and Watering Cans
Author: asb3967
Description:
[size=5][b]Durumi Hut 1.9.2 — detailed sprites and little watering cans[/b][/size]

[b]1.9.2 installation update[/b]
My 1.9.0 ZIP put a second mod manifest in a separate source folder, which could cause SMAPI to skip the mod. The 1.9.1 fix still kept the C# files in a separate subfolder. The new Main Files ZIP puts the source beside DurumiHut.dll and the single manifest in the existing DurumiHut folder.

Extract the whole ZIP directly into Mods, then start the game through SMAPI. I used AI-assisted testing to verify fresh installs and updates over an existing DurumiHut folder. The mod loaded and appeared in Robin's construction menu.

[b]한국어[/b] 1.9.0은 압축을 통째로 풀면 매니페스트가 중복돼 SMAPI가 모드를 건너뛸 수 있었습니다. 1.9.1에서도 소스는 별도 하위 폴더에 남겨뒀습니다. 이번 메인 ZIP은 기존 DurumiHut 폴더 안에 소스와 DLL, 매니페스트를 나란히 넣었습니다. ZIP 전체를 Mods에 한 번 풀고 SMAPI로 실행하세요. AI를 활용해 신규 설치와 기존 폴더 덮어쓰기를 실제 게임에서 검증했고, 로빈 건설 메뉴에서 두루미 오두막을 확인했습니다.

Red-bereted children share an illustrated home, help with crops, and spend their free time reading or playing nearby. Version 1.9 brings the newly designed character, festival clothing, work motions and reactions into the game. Existing huts and saved farming lessons are retained.

[b]New character artwork[/b]
The new artwork preserves Durumi's red beret, white bob with an asymmetric red forelock, black collar, split ivory tunic, detached sleeves, elbow guards, shorts, strapped knee pads and high-top shoes. The existing compact ten-year-old body scale is retained across front, side and back views.

Walking and carrying use the same dressed body frames. A separate little watering can attaches to the same right hand and follows the authored arm swing. In some far-side poses, the can is fully hidden by the child. Filling, pouring, harvesting, indoor activities and seasonal play use the new registered artwork. Artwork uses integer pixels and point sampling.

Walking follows eight phases tied to actual travel distance. Some cape and heavy-coat walks reuse authored poses within those eight phases. Brief greetings and a few front-facing attentive responses are available when the child can safely gesture. These are pixel animations with discrete poses; a general frame-rate or all-stutter performance guarantee is not claimed.

[b]Watering cans replace the old carried buckets[/b]
After the well upgrade, helpers fill a small can, carry it to a dry crop and pour before the soil becomes wet. Each fill still waters up to eight targets. The same maximum of three helpers handles both watering and harvesting.

Growing crops, trellis crops, wild seeds and outdoor garden pots are eligible. Empty soil, dead crops, wet soil and crops that need no water are skipped. A reachable route is required. The harvest toggle is independent of watering.

The 1.8.1 waypoint correction remains: consuming a path waypoint for one update retains the preceding travel picture. Version 1.9 also keeps the end of a harvest in the right outfit when rain begins, and prevents the previous harvest shake from carrying into later walking pictures. Actual movement speed, routes, collision and work timing keep their existing rules.

[b]Eight calendar festival outfits[/b]
The new dressed artwork includes a yellow garden apron, flower-pattern green vest, leaf-pattern summer shirt, navy jellyfish cape, harvest apron, purple Halloween cloak, blue quilted winter coat and red/green Winter Star duffle coat.

[list]
[*]Egg Festival: Spring 13[/*]
[*]Flower Dance: Spring 24[/*]
[*]Luau: Summer 11[/*]
[*]Dance of the Moonlight Jellies: Summer 28[/*]
[*]Stardew Valley Fair: Fall 16[/*]
[*]Spirit's Eve: Fall 27[/*]
[*]Festival of Ice: Winter 8[/*]
[*]Feast of the Winter Star: Winter 25[/*]
[/list]Passive festivals reuse related outfits: Desert Festival uses Fair, Trout Derby uses Luau, SquidFest uses Ice, and Night Market uses Winter Star. Native dates and unlock conditions apply. Outdoor raincoats take priority, winter clothing remains warm, and sleeping uses the normal hatless head. The children stay near their hut.

[b]The same children at home and in the field[/b]
Walk through the hut door to meet the helpers who work outside. They can read, turn pages, write, wash their hands, share a meal and settle beneath the quilt from 9 pm. The base hut has two children; an upgraded hut has three. Indoor and outdoor helpers form one population.

The illustrated room keeps its kitchen, dining table, canopy bed, bookcases, hearth, tea table and study. Chairs and bedding retain their foreground layers. Tall chair backs can cover much of a small seated child, including their hair and held props in some views. Meals and washing are visual routines; they do not consume crops or produce items.

The indoor harvest box opens shared 36-slot storage. The study control pauses or resumes harvesting. Inspect the globe, bookcase and stove for different lines. Furniture paths and the real doorway remain in use.

[b]Nearby interaction[/b]
Use the normal action button on a nearby child for a short response about the current activity. A bubble lasts about 2.6 seconds, with eight seconds between replies from the same child. Distance and walls limit interaction, and existing building and object actions take priority. Sleeping children remain asleep. Reactions are for the host's local player; multiplayer synchronization is unverified.

[b]Farming lessons[/b]
Use Durumi's face on the Farming row of the Skills page to teach the hut. The learned Farming level is two below the farmer's base level, capped at 8: a level 10 farmer teaches level 8. It affects native crop quality and level-dependent yield.

Work practice is a separate mod lesson: 4 percentage points per base Farming level, minus 20 percentage points, capped at a 20% action-time reduction. Thus a farmer's 40% reference becomes 20% for the child. This is a task-specific adaptation, not a vanilla Farming or Artisan action-speed bonus.

At taught level 8, normal picking takes about 1.6 seconds instead of 2; filling takes 720 ms instead of 900, and pouring takes 640 ms instead of 800. Preparation, commit and finish remain in sequence. Walking, range, crew size, eight-target capacity, fertilizer, storage and player stats retain their existing values. Saved lessons from earlier versions persist.

[b]Spare-time seasonal play[/b]
With no eligible work waiting, children can walk through the door to a clear, reachable 5×3 play area near the hut. Snowball play requires actual local winter snowfall and at least two available children. Summer bubbles require dry weather without lightning. Some children may remain indoors reading.

Short play bouts can begin at 10:00–11:30 or 14:00–17:30, followed by a break. New work, unsafe space, weather, dinner and bedtime take priority. Play adds no workers, output items, crop damage, combat damage or rewards. The helpers' work remains crop picking and watering.

[b]Rain, winter and festivals[/b]
Rainy mornings start indoors. If rain begins outdoors, helpers wear yellow raincoats and return through the door. Harvesters rest in rain, winter and on traditional festival days. The upgraded well's watering runs independently from 6 am to 7 pm on dry days, including winter and festivals when eligible crops need water. Rain stops watering. Outfit transition pictures do not create new rainy-day jobs.

[b]Build and upgrade[/b]
Robin offers the hut without wizard-quest, year or season unlocks. Normal shop hours and construction schedules apply. The original Junimo Hut remains available.

[list]
[*]Base: 13×13 area centered on the door, up to 2 helpers. Costs 20,000g, 200 stone, 9 starfruit and 100 fiber; takes 2 days.[/*]
[*]First upgrade: 17×17 area, up to 3 helpers. Costs 5,000g, 100 wood and 100 stone; takes 1 day.[/*]
[*]Well upgrade: same area and crew, plus physical watering. Costs 10,000g, 200 stone, 5 iron bars and 10 hardwood; takes 2 days.[/*]
[/list]Each exterior building occupies 3×2 tiles. The working area includes the building.

[b]Install and update[/b]
Install SMAPI 4.5.2 for Stardew Valley 1.6.15. Close the game and [b]extract the entire Main Files ZIP directly into your Mods folder[/b]. The C# source files sit beside DurumiHut.dll and manifest.json in Mods/DurumiHut. Extract over that folder to update an existing installation. For the standalone setup, use DurumiHut-Standalone/Mods. Launch through SMAPI. Content Patcher is not required.

If an earlier ZIP left a separate source/DurumiHut folder directly under Mods, move that old source copy out of Mods once. If SMAPI reports another duplicate Durumi Hut folder, keep the new Mods/DurumiHut and move only that duplicate outside Mods.

This standard ZIP includes the mod, source, assets, translations and build instructions. It contains no proprietary Stardew game files. Install SMAPI from [url=https://smapi.io/]its official site[/url].

The older optional Windows installer remains quarantined on Nexus. Its detections have not been established as false positives. Use the standard ZIP; do not bypass quarantine or disable protection for the old executable.

Items obstructed by room fixtures or the exit are recovered with their contents at the Mayor's Manor Lost and Found. A farmer loaded at an obsolete blocked position moves to the entrance. To uninstall, empty storage, leave the room, demolish all Durumi Huts through Robin while the mod is enabled, and save a day. Close the game, then remove the mod folder.

[b]Twelve languages[/b]
Construction, furniture, interactions and teaching follow the game's selected language: English, German, Spanish, French, Hungarian, Italian, Japanese, Korean, Brazilian Portuguese, Russian, Turkish and Simplified Chinese. Quick-start guides are included. Translations are AI-assisted; full native-speaker proofreading is not claimed.

[b]AI disclosure and credits[/b]
This is an unofficial Drami fan creation. Durumi is a user-defined ten-year-old child. The commissioning user supplied the character setting, Life Pack and illustrated room design. The player farmer and ordinary Junimos keep their original appearances.

OpenAI Codex and GPT-6 Astra assisted code, review, translations, documentation and testing. OpenAI's built-in image generation created or edited the original helper and hut artwork, followed by pixel registration and in-game inspection. AI-Generated Content and AI Media apply. Gameplay screenshots are actual captures; concept artwork is labelled. No endorsement by the game developer or streamer is claimed.

Stardew Valley belongs to ConcernedApe. SMAPI is maintained by Pathoschild and contributors. The mod loads game assets from the player's own installation.

[b]Validation and limits[/b]
Inspection covers Windows single-player with Stardew Valley 1.6.15 and SMAPI 4.5.2. Declared sprite and tool combinations are checked separately from actual helper behavior. Not every declared combination can occur during ordinary play. Multiplayer, other Junimo overhauls and every mod combination remain unverified. Please report reproducible problems with relevant SMAPI logs while keeping personal save and account data out of public posts.
